questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Event sources, event patterns, and event-driven response workflows
questions.text: A production account emits a GuardDuty finding for credential exfiltration. The security team wants the event to start an incident workflow without polling. Which event-driven design should be used?

answers.text: Use an EventBridge rule that matches GuardDuty finding events and targets an incident workflow
Schedule a daily script that searches for new findings
Ask analysts to refresh the GuardDuty console manually
Store the finding ID in a static parameter and wait for a deployment

explanations.a: GuardDuty findings are emitted as events, and EventBridge can route matching events directly to response automation or notification targets. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Daily polling delays response and does not use the event source that already exists.
explanations.c: Manual console checks are not reliable for time-sensitive incident response.
explanations.d: A static parameter does not route live security findings to responders.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Event sources, event patterns, and event-driven response workflows
questions.text: A DevOps team wants to detect CloudFormation stack failures and notify the application owner. What should the event pattern match?

answers.text: Only successful stack creation events
CloudFormation stack status change events for failed or rollback states
Only monthly billing events
Only S3 object lifecycle transition events

explanations.a: Successful events do not identify the failure condition that needs incident response.
explanations.b: Stack status events identify failed infrastructure changes and can be routed to the correct owner for response. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Billing events do not describe CloudFormation rollback status.
explanations.d: Lifecycle transitions do not indicate stack deployment failures.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Event sources, event patterns, and event-driven response workflows
questions.text: A company wants one response workflow for EC2 instance health failures and a different workflow for unauthorized IAM changes. What is the right pattern?

answers.text: Send every event to one generic target with no classification
Disable event matching and rely on a shared mailbox
Create separate event rules that match each event type and route to different targets
Use the EC2 instance name as the only event selector for IAM events

explanations.a: Generic routing makes ownership unclear and can increase response time.
explanations.b: A mailbox without structured routing does not preserve event type or priority reliably.
explanations.c: Different operational and security events need different owners, severity, and remediation paths. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Instance names do not identify IAM change events.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Event sources, event patterns, and event-driven response workflows
questions.text: A pipeline emits custom events when a release starts, succeeds, or fails. Which design makes those events useful for incident workflows?

answers.text: Put the entire event meaning only in a free-form message string
Use a different field schema for every service release
Include deployment secrets as event fields for convenience
Include stable detail fields such as service, environment, version, status, and owner

explanations.a: Free-form messages are harder to route and correlate than stable fields.
explanations.b: Inconsistent schemas make central event rules difficult to maintain.
explanations.c: Secrets should not be placed in operational events.
explanations.d: Structured event detail fields allow rules, dashboards, and incident tooling to route and correlate release events. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Event sources, event patterns, and event-driven response workflows
questions.text: An operations team receives too many EventBridge notifications because a rule matches all AWS API calls. What should be adjusted?

answers.text: Narrow the event pattern to specific sources, detail types, resources, or event names
Increase the number of responders on every alert
Delete all event rules and rely on memory
Match on random request IDs instead of event meaning

explanations.a: Specific event patterns reduce noise and make incident response events actionable. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: More responders do not fix noisy event selection.
explanations.c: Removing event rules eliminates automated detection.
explanations.d: Random identifiers do not represent stable incident conditions.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Event sources, event patterns, and event-driven response workflows
questions.text: A remediation target should run only for events from production accounts. What should the event-driven response include?

answers.text: A target that ignores event account identity
Account or environment filtering in the event pattern or routing layer
A response that treats all sandbox events as critical production incidents
A rule that matches only the event timestamp format

explanations.a: Ignoring account identity can trigger the wrong response path.
explanations.b: Filtering by account or environment prevents nonproduction events from triggering production response workflows. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Equal severity for sandbox and production creates alert fatigue.
explanations.d: Timestamp format does not identify the affected environment.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Incident severity, ownership, escalation, and communication
questions.text: A database outage affects customer checkout globally. Which incident classification is most appropriate?

answers.text: Low-priority ticket for the next planning meeting
Silent remediation with no communication record
High-severity incident with immediate escalation to service owners and leadership communications
Developer-only notification with no service owner involvement

explanations.a: A global checkout outage cannot wait for normal planning cycles.
explanations.b: Major incidents need communication and evidence, not silent action only.
explanations.c: Customer-impacting global checkout failure requires urgent response, clear ownership, and coordinated communication. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Service owners and response leads are needed for business-impacting outages.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Incident severity, ownership, escalation, and communication
questions.text: A warning alarm fires for a noncritical batch job that retries successfully. What response model is most appropriate?

answers.text: Page the entire company for every retry
Ignore the condition forever because it recovered once
Treat the event as a security breach without evidence
Lower-severity notification or ticket with no immediate page if service objectives are not at risk

explanations.a: Escalating every transient retry creates noise and reduces trust in alerts.
explanations.b: Recovered warnings can still deserve trend tracking or follow-up.
explanations.c: A retrying batch job is not automatically a security incident.
explanations.d: Incident severity should reflect impact and urgency so responders are not paged for noncritical self-recovered conditions. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Incident severity, ownership, escalation, and communication
questions.text: During a major incident, two teams make conflicting changes to the same production service. What incident-management role or process would reduce this risk?

answers.text: Assign an incident commander and define a change coordination channel
Let every engineer independently apply fixes as quickly as possible
Disable all communication until after the outage
Rotate AWS account aliases to identify the commander

explanations.a: A single coordination role and channel reduce conflicting actions and maintain a controlled response timeline. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Uncoordinated changes can worsen impact and obscure root cause.
explanations.c: Communication is needed during response to coordinate actions.
explanations.d: Account aliases do not coordinate incident decisions.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Incident severity, ownership, escalation, and communication
questions.text: An alert message says only 'ALARM' with no service, Region, owner, or runbook. What should be improved?

answers.text: Remove the alarm name as well
Notification context and escalation metadata
Send the same empty message to more channels
Add credentials to the message body

explanations.a: Less context makes response slower.
explanations.b: Responders need affected service, scope, severity, owner, and runbook details to take timely action. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: More channels do not compensate for missing action context.
explanations.d: Secrets should not be included in notifications.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Incident severity, ownership, escalation, and communication
questions.text: A security finding affects one development account, but production is not exposed. How should the event be handled?

answers.text: Suppress all development security findings permanently
Escalate as a full production outage without considering scope
Route to the security owner with severity based on impact and exposure
Send only to application customers

explanations.a: Development findings can still indicate risk and should be tracked appropriately.
explanations.b: Incorrect severity can waste response capacity and reduce alert credibility.
explanations.c: Severity and escalation should reflect environment, exposure, and risk while still ensuring security ownership. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Customers usually do not need notification for an isolated development-account finding.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Incident severity, ownership, escalation, and communication
questions.text: A team needs to notify executives during major incidents but not for every technical alarm. What should determine executive communication?

answers.text: Every CloudWatch datapoint breach regardless of impact
Only whether the alarm name is alphabetically first
Only the size of the deployment artifact
Severity, customer impact, and incident communication policy

explanations.a: Raw datapoint breaches can be noisy and do not always require executive notification.
explanations.b: Alphabetical order has no relationship to business impact.
explanations.c: Artifact size does not determine executive escalation.
explanations.d: Executive updates should be tied to meaningful business impact and defined communication thresholds. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Automated remediation and runbook orchestration
questions.text: A memory leak causes ECS tasks to fail after several hours. The team wants an automated response that restarts tasks only after a verified alarm. Which pattern should be used?

answers.text: CloudWatch alarm routed to EventBridge or service automation with scoped remediation
A script that restarts every service every minute
Manual restarts with no runbook or evidence
A public endpoint that lets anyone restart tasks

explanations.a: Alarm-driven automation can invoke a controlled action when telemetry confirms the unhealthy condition. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Unbounded restarts can create instability and hide the real problem.
explanations.c: Manual undocumented restarts are slower and harder to audit.
explanations.d: Unauthenticated restart capability creates operational and security risk.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Automated remediation and runbook orchestration
questions.text: A runbook stops and starts instances to remediate a known kernel issue. What should be included to make it production-safe?

answers.text: Wildcard target selection with no preview
Approvals, target validation, error handling, and execution logging
Suppressed logs for every execution
Permanent administrator credentials embedded in the script

explanations.a: Unvalidated wildcard targeting can affect unintended instances.
explanations.b: Production remediation needs guardrails that confirm scope, handle failures, and preserve an audit record. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Missing logs make it harder to prove what happened during remediation.
explanations.d: Embedded broad credentials increase exposure and complicate rotation.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Automated remediation and runbook orchestration
questions.text: An automated remediation repeatedly triggers for the same symptom without resolving it. What control should be added?

answers.text: Infinite retries with no delay
Deletion of the alarm after the first attempt
Cooldowns, maximum attempts, and escalation to humans
Randomly changing unrelated settings on each retry

explanations.a: Infinite retries can amplify instability and waste resources.
explanations.b: Deleting detection hides the continuing incident.
explanations.c: Automation should stop repeated ineffective actions and escalate when the condition persists. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Unrelated changes make the system less predictable and harder to diagnose.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Automated remediation and runbook orchestration
questions.text: A remediation workflow must isolate an EC2 instance suspected of compromise while preserving evidence. Which action is appropriate?

answers.text: Terminate the instance immediately with no snapshot or logs
Open inbound SSH to the internet for faster access
Delete CloudTrail events related to the instance
Apply a restrictive security group and snapshot relevant volumes before deeper analysis

explanations.a: Immediate termination can destroy evidence needed for root cause and forensic analysis.
explanations.b: Opening access increases risk during a suspected compromise.
explanations.c: Audit evidence should be preserved, not deleted.
explanations.d: Network containment limits exposure while snapshots preserve data for investigation. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Automated remediation and runbook orchestration
questions.text: A team wants automated remediation to run across accounts. What is the safest access model?

answers.text: Assume least-privilege remediation roles in target accounts
Store every account root password in the automation document
Use one developer's long-term access key everywhere
Make target resources public during remediation

explanations.a: Cross-account response should use scoped roles that grant only the actions needed for the runbook. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Root passwords should not be stored or used for routine automation.
explanations.c: Shared long-term keys weaken accountability and increase blast radius.
explanations.d: Public exposure is not an access model for safe remediation.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Knowledge: Automated remediation and runbook orchestration
questions.text: A runbook remediates public S3 bucket policies. What should it do before changing policies automatically?

answers.text: Overwrite every bucket policy in the account without checking the finding
Capture current policy, verify the bucket matches the finding, and log the intended change
Skip logging so the remediation is faster
Delete the bucket first to remove the finding

explanations.a: Broad overwrites can break unrelated workloads.
explanations.b: Safe remediation confirms target scope and preserves before-state evidence for review and rollback. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Missing logs reduce accountability and complicate post-incident analysis.
explanations.d: Deleting data is a destructive response and may violate retention requirements.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Creating EventBridge rules for operational and security events
questions.text: A team wants to detect IAM policy changes that grant AdministratorAccess outside the identity pipeline. Which EventBridge pattern is appropriate?

answers.text: Match only EC2 instance state-change events
Match only S3 object-created events in artifact buckets
Match CloudTrail IAM policy attachment or policy version events and filter for high-risk changes
Match only CodeBuild phase-change events

explanations.a: Instance state changes do not identify IAM policy changes.
explanations.b: Object-created events do not show IAM authorization changes.
explanations.c: IAM management events from CloudTrail can be routed through EventBridge for near-real-time detection of permission changes. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Build phase events do not detect out-of-band IAM policy changes.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Creating EventBridge rules for operational and security events
questions.text: An Auto Scaling group emits an EC2 instance launch failure event. The platform team wants a ticket created with the group name. What should be configured?

answers.text: A static ticket created once per quarter
An unrelated Route 53 health check
A manual search of console notifications at the end of the day
EventBridge rule matching Auto Scaling events and a target that maps event details into the ticket

explanations.a: A static ticket does not capture live launch failures.
explanations.b: DNS health checks do not include Auto Scaling failure details.
explanations.c: Manual end-of-day review delays response to capacity issues.
explanations.d: Auto Scaling lifecycle and failure events contain context that can be routed into incident systems. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Creating EventBridge rules for operational and security events
questions.text: A CloudTrail event shows StopLogging was called for a trail. Which EventBridge response is appropriate?

answers.text: Notify security responders and invoke a controlled runbook to re-enable or investigate logging
Ignore the event because CloudTrail records only old activity
Delete the log archive bucket to prevent confusion
Treat it only as a normal application performance alert

explanations.a: Stopping audit logging is high risk and should trigger both notification and controlled response. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: CloudTrail events can represent recent account activity and logging tampering matters.
explanations.c: Deleting log storage destroys evidence.
explanations.d: Audit logging tampering has security and compliance implications.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Creating EventBridge rules for operational and security events
questions.text: A deployment pipeline should emit a custom event when production rollback starts. What should the event include?

answers.text: Only a vague message saying something changed
Service, environment, version, rollback reason, and execution ID
Production database passwords for rapid debugging
Only the developer's local machine name

explanations.a: Vague events slow correlation and ownership decisions.
explanations.b: Structured rollback events let responders correlate release impact and track remediation progress. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Secrets must not be included in event payloads.
explanations.d: Local machine names do not identify release scope or rollback cause.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Creating EventBridge rules for operational and security events
questions.text: An organization wants to route AWS Health events for affected services to different application teams. What should the EventBridge workflow use?

answers.text: The alphabetical order of team names
Only a single catch-all mailbox with no routing
Event detail fields such as service, event type, account, and Region to route ownership
The number of log groups in the account

explanations.a: Alphabetical routing is not tied to service ownership or event scope.
explanations.b: Catch-all routing can delay the team responsible for the affected service.
explanations.c: AWS Health event details can be used to determine which team and runbook should receive the notification. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Log group count does not identify which service is affected by the Health event.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Creating EventBridge rules for operational and security events
questions.text: A security remediation should run only when a Config rule reports NON_COMPLIANT for a specific resource type. What should the event rule match?

answers.text: All Config events regardless of rule and status
Only successful deployment events
Only daily billing alerts
Config compliance change events with the target rule name, resource type, and NON_COMPLIANT status

explanations.a: Matching all events can trigger remediation for unrelated or compliant resources.
explanations.b: Deployment success does not identify the Config noncompliance condition.
explanations.c: Billing alerts do not describe resource compliance changes.
explanations.d: Specific Config event patterns prevent remediation from acting on unrelated compliance changes. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Configuring notifications, ticketing, and chat integrations
questions.text: A production alarm should create a ticket, page on-call, and post context to a chat channel. Which integration model is appropriate?

answers.text: Route the alarm through SNS or EventBridge to incident management and chat targets
Place the alarm ARN only in a wiki page
Ask users to report outages through support before notifying on-call
Send the alarm only to an unmonitored email alias

explanations.a: Alarm events can fan out to notification, ticketing, and collaboration tools to start coordinated response. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: A wiki page does not actively notify responders or create incidents.
explanations.c: User reports are a delayed and incomplete detection path.
explanations.d: Unmonitored aliases do not provide reliable incident response.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Configuring notifications, ticketing, and chat integrations
questions.text: An incident notification lacks Region, account, and runbook link. What should be added?

answers.text: Remove the metric name to shorten the alert
Message enrichment with affected resource, scope, severity, owner, and runbook
Add secrets so responders can copy them faster
Send only a screenshot with no text fields

explanations.a: Removing key context makes the alert less actionable.
explanations.b: Enriched notifications help responders triage quickly and choose the correct response procedure. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Secrets should not be included in notifications.
explanations.d: Screenshots are hard to search and automate compared with structured fields.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Configuring notifications, ticketing, and chat integrations
questions.text: A chat integration receives repeated messages for the same alarm every minute during an outage. What should be implemented?

answers.text: Create a separate high-priority ticket for every datapoint
Disable the alarm forever after the first message
Deduplication or incident aggregation based on alarm and resource identity
Route repeated messages to random teams

explanations.a: Per-datapoint tickets flood responders and obscure the incident.
explanations.b: Permanent alarm deletion removes future detection.
explanations.c: Grouping repeated signals reduces alert fatigue and keeps responders focused on one incident thread. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Random routing increases confusion and delays ownership.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Configuring notifications, ticketing, and chat integrations
questions.text: A low-severity event should create a ticket but not page the primary on-call engineer. What should control this behavior?

answers.text: One paging policy for every informational event
No ticket creation for low-severity operational drift
Routing based only on resource name length
Severity-based notification routing

explanations.a: Paging for all informational events creates noise.
explanations.b: Low-severity drift can still require trackable follow-up.
explanations.c: Name length does not represent impact or urgency.
explanations.d: Severity routing maps events to the right urgency and channel. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Configuring notifications, ticketing, and chat integrations
questions.text: A team wants ticket updates when an automated runbook succeeds or fails. What should the automation emit?

answers.text: Structured status events or API updates containing execution ID and outcome
Only local console output from the runbook
Only a changed dashboard color
Only a new IAM role name

explanations.a: Execution status updates let ticketing systems track remediation progress and final state. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Local output may not reach the incident record.
explanations.c: Dashboard color changes do not update the ticket history.
explanations.d: Role names do not communicate runbook outcome.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Configuring notifications, ticketing, and chat integrations
questions.text: A security incident requires a private response channel with restricted membership. What should the notification design support?

answers.text: Posting all sensitive findings in a public company channel
Routing sensitive incidents to restricted security channels or ticket queues
Sending findings to application customers by default
Embedding full access keys in chat for convenience

explanations.a: Public channels can expose security-sensitive details to unnecessary audiences.
explanations.b: Sensitive findings should be visible only to authorized responders while preserving response tracking. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Customers should not receive raw internal security findings by default.
explanations.d: Access keys should never be posted in incident channels.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Implementing Systems Manager Automation runbooks for response
questions.text: A Systems Manager Automation document restarts a service on EC2 instances. What should the runbook use to target the correct instances safely?

answers.text: Wildcard all instances in all accounts by default
Manual instance IDs copied from memory
Tags or resource groups with validation of the intended environment
A public list of private IP addresses

explanations.a: A broad wildcard target can restart unrelated or production-critical systems.
explanations.b: Memory-based selection is error-prone and not repeatable.
explanations.c: Tag-based targeting with validation reduces the chance of running remediation against the wrong fleet. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Public lists can expose infrastructure details and are not a safe targeting control.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Implementing Systems Manager Automation runbooks for response
questions.text: A runbook must approve a disruptive database failover step before execution. Which Systems Manager Automation feature is relevant?

answers.text: Unconditional execution of every step
Hidden execution logs
Randomized step ordering
Approval step

explanations.a: Unconditional disruptive actions can cause avoidable impact.
explanations.b: Hidden logs reduce auditability and do not provide approval.
explanations.c: Random step ordering makes runbook behavior unsafe and unpredictable.
explanations.d: Approval steps allow controlled human authorization before a high-impact action proceeds. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Implementing Systems Manager Automation runbooks for response
questions.text: An automation runbook should be reusable across accounts and Regions. What should be parameterized?

answers.text: Target account, Region, resource IDs, and environment-specific values
The runbook should hardcode the first production resource it ever remediated
The runbook should infer targets from the operator's laptop name
The runbook should require editing source code for every execution

explanations.a: Parameterization avoids hardcoded targets and supports controlled reuse across environments. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Hardcoded production targets can affect the wrong resource during later executions.
explanations.c: Laptop names are not reliable resource selectors.
explanations.d: Editing runbook code for each execution increases risk and reduces repeatability.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Implementing Systems Manager Automation runbooks for response
questions.text: A remediation document needs permissions to stop and start EC2 instances but not modify IAM. What role design is best?

answers.text: AdministratorAccess because remediation is urgent
Automation assume role with only the required EC2 actions on approved resources
No role and embedded access keys in the document
A role that allows IAM policy deletion for every resource

explanations.a: Broad permissions increase blast radius beyond the runbook's purpose.
explanations.b: A least-privilege automation role limits what the runbook can do if invoked incorrectly. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Embedded keys are difficult to protect and rotate.
explanations.d: IAM deletion rights are unrelated to stopping and starting EC2 instances.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Implementing Systems Manager Automation runbooks for response
questions.text: A runbook fails halfway through and leaves a resource in maintenance mode. What should the runbook include?

answers.text: No error handling because automation should be perfect
Delete execution history after failure
Failure handling, rollback or cleanup steps, and final status reporting
Continue with destructive steps even when prerequisites fail

explanations.a: Automation can fail and must handle partial execution safely.
explanations.b: Execution history is needed to diagnose and audit the partial failure.
explanations.c: Runbooks need predictable cleanup and status reporting so partial failure does not leave services impaired. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Proceeding after failed prerequisites can worsen the incident.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.1 Skill: Implementing Systems Manager Automation runbooks for response
questions.text: A team wants to trigger the same Systems Manager runbook from alarms and from manual incident response. What should they ensure?

answers.text: The runbook produces different random changes each time
The runbook has no execution logging
The runbook ignores current resource state
The runbook is idempotent and records who or what invoked each execution

explanations.a: Random outcomes are unsafe for repeatable response.
explanations.b: Without logging, manual and automated invocations cannot be audited.
explanations.c: Ignoring state can cause unnecessary or unsafe actions.
explanations.d: Idempotency supports safe repeated execution, and invocation context preserves accountability. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Root cause analysis, timelines, and evidence preservation
questions.text: A production incident is resolved, but the team needs a reliable root-cause timeline. What evidence should be preserved?

answers.text: Alarm state changes, deployment events, logs, traces, CloudTrail events, and remediation actions
Only the final incident summary with no timestamps
Only screenshots stored on one responder's laptop
Only the cost report for the month

explanations.a: A complete timeline requires operational signals, release context, audit events, and response actions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: A summary without timestamps cannot reconstruct sequence or causality.
explanations.c: Personal screenshots are incomplete and fragile as incident evidence.
explanations.d: Cost data alone does not explain incident sequence or technical cause.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Root cause analysis, timelines, and evidence preservation
questions.text: A suspected compromise is detected on an EC2 instance. What evidence-preserving action should happen before rebuilding when feasible?

answers.text: Terminate the instance immediately with no records
Snapshot affected volumes and preserve relevant logs and CloudTrail events
Delete CloudTrail events to prevent confusion
Open the instance to the internet for easier investigation

explanations.a: Immediate destruction can remove evidence needed to determine scope and cause.
explanations.b: Snapshots and logs provide evidence for analysis while allowing containment and recovery to proceed. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Audit events should be preserved, not deleted.
explanations.d: Opening access increases risk during a security investigation.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Root cause analysis, timelines, and evidence preservation
questions.text: A team wants to know whether a bad deployment or a dependency outage caused errors. What timeline evidence is most useful?

answers.text: Only the number of developers online
Only the size of the deployment artifact
Deployment timestamps correlated with service metrics, logs, traces, and dependency health events
Only the length of the incident title

explanations.a: Responder availability does not establish technical root cause.
explanations.b: Artifact size alone rarely explains user-facing errors.
explanations.c: Time correlation helps distinguish release-induced failures from external dependency problems. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Title length has no causal diagnostic value.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Root cause analysis, timelines, and evidence preservation
questions.text: An incident response automation changes security groups to contain a host. What evidence should be captured?

answers.text: Only the name of the chat channel
Only a note that something was fixed
Only the unrelated application version list
Before-and-after security group rules, target resource IDs, execution ID, and actor

explanations.a: Channel name does not prove which resources were changed.
explanations.b: A vague note lacks the technical details needed for review.
explanations.c: Application versions do not document the containment change.
explanations.d: Capturing the change details preserves accountability and supports later review of containment actions. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Root cause analysis, timelines, and evidence preservation

answers.text: Align log retention with incident investigation and compliance requirements
Reduce retention further to lower evidence volume
Rely only on memory during post-incident review
Disable logging so missing logs are expected

explanations.a: Retention windows should preserve evidence long enough for realistic detection, response, and review timelines. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Shorter retention worsens the evidence gap.
explanations.c: Human memory is incomplete and not auditable.
explanations.d: No logging removes evidence needed for operations and compliance.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

Contributing factors, detection gaps, control gaps, and corrective actions
A list of unrelated services not involved in the incident
Removing all automation because one runbook failed

explanations.c: Unrelated services do not help explain or prevent the incident.
explanations.d: A failed runbook should be improved with evidence, not automatically abandoned.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

DNS record name length

explanations.b: Branch count does not measure incident detection.
explanations.c: Mean time to detect measures how long it takes to identify an incident after it begins. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

Mean time to recover

explanations.c: AMI creation date does not describe service restoration time.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

It should avoid all ownership to stay blameless
It should be stored only in a private notebook

explanations.b: The issue is the lack of detail and accountability.
explanations.c: Blameless reviews still need accountable owners for improvements.
explanations.d: Private notes do not provide trackable organizational follow-up.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Incident metrics, post-incident review, and continuous improvement

A larger incident bridge with no technical change
A manual reminder to be careful with no enforcement

explanations.b: Post-incident learning should feed changes into automation, tests, alarms, or release gates. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: More meeting capacity does not prevent the deployment defect.
explanations.d: Reminders are weaker than improved controls or automation.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Incident metrics, post-incident review, and continuous improvement
questions.text: A monthly report should show whether incident response is improving. Which measurements are useful?

Only the longest log message length
Incident count, severity distribution, MTTD, MTTR, recurrence, and action-item completion
Only the count of unused IAM roles

explanations.a: Dashboard count does not prove response outcomes improved.
explanations.b: Log message length does not measure incident response performance.
explanations.c: These metrics show reliability trends, response speed, repeat problems, and whether improvements are being delivered. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Unused role count may matter for security hygiene but not incident response trend by itself.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Knowledge: Incident metrics, post-incident review, and continuous improvement
questions.text: A post-incident review identifies alert fatigue as a contributing factor. What improvement is appropriate?

explanations.b: Removing all alerts delays detection of real incidents.

explanations.d: Reducing nonactionable noise helps responders notice and act on important signals. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Investigating incidents with logs, metrics, traces, and audit events

Only review the billing dashboard
Only count the number of pull requests open
Only check whether the domain name is short

explanations.b: Cost data alone does not explain API 5XX behavior.

explanations.d: Domain length has no diagnostic value for 5XX errors.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

Only the latest container image scan result

explanations.c: IAM group names do not show query performance.
explanations.d: Image scanning does not diagnose database query latency.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Investigating incidents with logs, metrics, traces, and audit events

Only ALB access logs

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Investigating incidents with logs, metrics, traces, and audit events

explanations.b: Object lifecycle transitions do not show consumer progress.
explanations.c: Contact metadata does not diagnose message processing delay.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Investigating incidents with logs, metrics, traces, and audit events
questions.text: A Lambda function error rate increases only for one alias during a canary deployment. What should be compared?

Only DNS query logs for static content

explanations.b: EC2 CPU does not isolate Lambda canary version behavior.
explanations.c: EBS volume size does not explain Lambda alias errors.
explanations.d: Static DNS query logs do not identify Lambda version-specific failures.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Investigating incidents with logs, metrics, traces, and audit events
questions.text: An intermittent user issue has a correlation ID. The logs are spread across services and accounts. What should the investigation use?

Only a count of deployed stacks

explanations.a: Unfiltered broad searches are slow and noisy.

explanations.c: A distributed issue may originate in an earlier service.
explanations.d: Stack count does not show request-specific behavior.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Capturing incident timelines and remediation evidence
questions.text: An incident commander wants an accurate timeline of response actions. What should be recorded automatically where possible?

answers.text: Only a final message that the incident ended
Only the number of people in the chat channel
Alarm times, acknowledgments, runbook executions, deployment changes, and status updates
Only the length of the incident call

explanations.b: Participant count does not capture technical actions.
explanations.c: A timeline built from system events and response actions supports review and accountability. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Call length does not document remediation steps or cause.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Capturing incident timelines and remediation evidence
questions.text: A runbook made a production change during an incident. What evidence should be attached to the incident record?

answers.text: Only the runbook title with no execution data
Only the responder's opinion that it worked
Only unrelated service dashboards
Runbook execution ID, parameters, actor, target resources, and outcome

explanations.a: A title does not prove what occurred in a specific execution.
explanations.b: Subjective statements should be supported by execution and validation evidence.
explanations.c: Unrelated dashboards do not document the runbook action.
explanations.d: Execution metadata shows what automation did, where it acted, and whether it succeeded. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Capturing incident timelines and remediation evidence
questions.text: A manual console change is made to restore service. What should the responder do for evidence and follow-up?

answers.text: Record the change, capture related CloudTrail events, and create an action item to codify it if needed
Leave the change undocumented because the service recovered
Delete the CloudTrail records to keep the timeline simple
Repeat the manual change in every environment without review

explanations.a: Manual emergency changes should be documented and later reconciled into controlled automation or IaC. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Undocumented changes create drift and weaken post-incident learning.
explanations.c: Audit records should be preserved, not removed.
explanations.d: Emergency action should be reviewed before broad replication.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Capturing incident timelines and remediation evidence

Time source, timezone, and timestamp format in incident records
No timestamps to avoid disagreement
Only relative terms such as earlier and later

explanations.a: Uncoordinated time formats make timelines harder to interpret.
explanations.b: Consistent timestamp handling prevents confusion when reconstructing sequence across systems. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Removing timestamps makes root-cause analysis much weaker.
explanations.d: Relative terms are less precise than standardized timestamps.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Capturing incident timelines and remediation evidence
questions.text: A remediation automation should prove that service health recovered. What should it capture after the action?

answers.text: Only that the automation started
Only the original alarm state with no recheck
Validation metrics or checks showing the affected service returned to an acceptable state
Only the source repository URL

explanations.a: Start status does not prove successful remediation.
explanations.b: The original alarm does not show recovery after action.
explanations.c: Evidence of post-action health confirms whether remediation resolved the incident. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Repository location does not validate service recovery.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Capturing incident timelines and remediation evidence

Only screenshots with no linked events or actions
Only the name of the AWS account
Severity, impact, timeline, responders, evidence, corrective actions, and approvals for risky steps

explanations.b: Screenshots alone are incomplete and difficult to audit.
explanations.c: Account name alone does not describe impact, timeline, or response.
explanations.d: Compliance-oriented incident records need enough context to show what happened, who acted, and how controls were followed. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Updating runbooks and controls after incidents
questions.text: A post-incident review finds the runbook told responders to check the wrong log group. What should be done?

answers.text: Update the runbook and validate it in a game day or test execution

Delete the runbook because it had one error
Move the correct log group name into a private note only

explanations.a: Runbook corrections should be tested so responders can trust the procedure during the next incident. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Memory-based fixes do not help future responders.
explanations.c: A flawed runbook should be improved rather than discarded automatically.
explanations.d: Private notes do not update the shared operational procedure.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

explanations.c: Secret names do not ensure alarms watch the right resource.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

explanations.d: Removing metrics makes future detection harder.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.2 Skill: Updating runbooks and controls after incidents

explanations.c: Dashboard layout polish does not prove alarm actionability.
explanations.d: Manual checking does not validate automated alerting.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

explanations.c: Responders still need a safe path to restore service.
explanations.d: Hiding the policy prevents governance rather than improving it.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

explanations.c: Monitoring is needed to detect real impact from the change.
explanations.d: Descriptions are not sufficient change coordination or rollback control.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

explanations.b: Billing owners are not usually responsible for network exposure response.
explanations.c: Audit logs are especially important during infrastructure changes.
explanations.d: Security group changes can alter exposure and should be monitored or remediated according to policy. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

questions.name: Incident and Event Response

Keep applying the failed template until it succeeds
Delete the VPC to remove the bad route

explanations.a: Stack rollback restores the prior infrastructure definition, and validation confirms service recovery. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Unrecorded manual edits create drift and complicate root cause.
explanations.c: Repeatedly applying an invalid route can prolong the outage.
explanations.d: Deleting the VPC is destructive and unnecessary for route rollback.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.3 Skill: Automating safe rollback and containment actions
questions.text: A queue consumer release creates poison messages. How should containment protect the rest of the system?

answers.text: Purge the queue immediately without evidence
Pause or roll back the consumer and route failed messages to a DLQ for inspection
Increase consumer concurrency dramatically
Disable the DLQ to keep the main queue clean

explanations.a: Purging can lose valid business events and remove diagnostic data.
explanations.b: Stopping the bad processor and isolating failed messages prevents further damage while preserving payloads. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: More consumers can amplify the bad processing behavior.
explanations.d: Removing the DLQ reduces failure isolation.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.3 Skill: Automating safe rollback and containment actions
questions.text: A bad feature flag rollout affects only 20% of users. What automated response is appropriate?

answers.text: Rebuild every AMI before changing the flag
Expand the rollout to all users for consistency
Roll back or disable the feature flag through the configuration deployment system
Delete all configuration history

explanations.a: A feature flag incident can often be contained faster through configuration rollback.
explanations.b: Expanding a bad flag increases impact.
explanations.c: Feature-flag rollback can contain the incident quickly without rebuilding application artifacts. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: History is needed to understand and audit the rollback.

questions.name: Incident and Event Response
questions.objective: Task 5.3 Skill: Automating safe rollback and containment actions
questions.text: A rollback automation should not proceed if the previous version is also unhealthy. What safety check is required?

answers.text: Always roll back blindly regardless of target state
Use the oldest artifact in the repository by default
Choose rollback targets based on file name length
Pre-rollback validation of rollback target health and availability

explanations.a: Blind rollback can move users to another broken version.
explanations.b: The oldest artifact may be incompatible or insecure.
explanations.c: File name length does not indicate health or compatibility.
explanations.d: Rollback should move traffic only to a version or environment that is known to be healthy enough to serve. This is the correct answer.
